text.p: Valores Finamex said on Friday it downgraded Mexican corn tortilla giant Grupo Maseca to market performer from buy.
"Under the current environment of low government-subsidy ceilings and dropping corn prices, such premiums for Maseca are not justified," analyst Francisco Rivero said in a report.
He said the stock is trading at premiums of up to 24 percent on the basis of estimated earnings for 1997 and 1998 and EBITDA compared to an average of stocks the brokerage covers.
A change in the Mexican government's subsidy scheme on corn tortillas could provide a boost for the company, Rivero said, adding such a change does not seem likely in the near future.
He forecast a 31 percent decrease in sales in 1997 and a decline in operating income while operating margins expand.
The brokerage estimates earnings per share for Maseca in 1997 at 0.588 peso and for 1998 0.535 peso.
Maseca's Series B shares fell four centavos to 7.44 pesos on Thursday, while its ADRs fell 1/8 to 14-1/4 in New York.
